We will start the management commentary followed by a Q&A session to discuss the financial

Suresh Iyer: 
Thank you, Nidhesh, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining the earnings call for 
the second quarter results of Can Fin Homes. Before we get into the questionnaire, I do have a 
small brief on the highlights of the quarter, which I will just share and then we can go into the 
question-answers.  
 
The highlight of the quarter for Can Fin, obviously, has been that the entire Project Tejas, which 
is the IT transformation project, has gone fully live. In fact, we went in phases where July, we 
went ahead with 11 branches, five old branches and six new branches. Thereafter, in the month 
of August, additional 75 old branches and 14 new branches were added. In the month of 
September, 77 old branches were again were added, and finally from effective 1st of October, 
93 of the remaining old branches and the five branches which were subsequently opened, new 
branches, have all gone live.  
 
Presently, we are completely online in the new system. All the aspects of the project, including 
the security aspect, the infrastructure aspects which were already implemented earlier, and now 
all the operational or functionalities which are there in the project have all been implemented, 
and we have gone live with the entire LOS, LMS across all the branches.  
 
Of course, this implementation has had an impact in terms of our disbursement, particularly in 
each of the branches in the month where the business has or the IT implementation has taken 
place. To this effect, we have actually given an additional slide in the presentation, that is Slide 
number 20, as to the impact that we have had because of this IT implementation.  
 
The month in which the implementation has happened, the disbursements, they have dropped in 
that particular branches by about 70% to 75%, and then the next month, again, it pushes back 
and it comes back to almost 80%-90% of the old disbursement. That's the kind of thing. As a 
result of this, in the month particularly of August and September, where we had a large chunk

of 75 and 77 old branches going live, there has been a major impact and as a result, the 
disbursements for the quarter were at only INR2,375 crores.  
 
This, of course, is net of the INR29 crores which we have reduced from the disbursements 
because of the NHB guidelines which have come saying that regarding the cancellation of DDs. 
During the quarter, we've had about INR28, odd crores of cancellations of disbursements, which 
were earlier handed over to customers for various reasons, and that has been netted off. 
 
Plus, also about INR19 lakhs was in respect of the cancellations from the date of the closure of 
the quarter to the date of announcement of the results. Basically, combined, both these things 
put together is about INR29 crores, which has also been netted off from this INR2,375 crores. 
That is the impact.  
 
In terms of the state-wise or region-wise disbursement, the demand has been almost has been 
quite strong. There has been no change in that demand. We observed that. In fact, on Page 20 of 
the presentation, you will also see that particularly the branches where no impact or no the IT 
transformation has happened in the month of October, there you will see that in the month of 
July, August and September, the business has been robust. There has been an increase only. As 
against an average of 435 crores which these 93 branches were doing in Q1, in the month of 
September also they've done average of 454, 458, 424 and 481 crores.  
 
Basically, in terms of the demand or in terms of the business per se, there has been no change, 
but for the impact of the IT transformation, which is mainly on account of the understanding, or 
rather the change in the flow, the additional processes that have been incorporated. Now, in fact, 
there are some four OTPs, four to five OTPs, depending on the customer and the type, which we 
have to take from that borrower as well as the co-borrower separately. 
 
That comes to around 8 to 10 OTPs additionally. So that is a those kind of process changes which 
have been implemented have resulted in some time lag and things like that. Plus, in every month, 
since it was a migration from a legacy system, the data had to go through a couple of processes. 
Every month, we basically were able to hand over to the branches only after post-5th. That five 
days of gap also.  
 
Basically, these are one-time issues which have impacted, but as can be seen from the 93 
branches data, the demand is there is no issue. We are still seeing a robust demand across all the 
geographies. Karnataka also, which has been in the past always a point of observation, has 
stabilized around INR230 to INR250 crores of disbursement consistently.  
 
The only other change during the quarter has been that in the state of Telangana, there's been a 
new Section 22 or something some Section has been wherein, at the time of some areas have 
been identified by the sub-registrar offices or by the government to have been like notified for 
this, which is only available with the sub-registrar offices. 
 
Before execution of any document, everything has to be taken to the sub-registrar office, and 
they will confirm whether this can be registered or cannot be registered. This process, before the 
entire process of processing, we had a lot of cases where finally when it went for the

documentation or registration, the process was stopped because then, some study or as per 
Section 22, the legality of those properties is being verified again.

now before we entertain any login or spend time in processing the entire case, we ask the 
customer only to get the item verified from the sub-registrar office and then only do it. 
Otherwise, a lot of cases where it came all the effort up to the stage of documentation was done, 
and we had to cancel the disbursement. Basically, that process has been changed now to adjust 
to this new change of Section 22.  
 
As a result of this, this was only a one-quarter impact, which is there in terms of disbursement. 
For the full year, we continue to have the same guidance of INR13,000 crores in terms of 
disbursement. To that effect, whatever corrections, whatever strengthening we have had to do, 
we have already initiated in October itself across all the branches, so that we can push 
disbursements in Q3 and Q4.  
 
Another thing is that now with the entire all branches having gone on the new system, we should 
now be able to pull out the people from the teams for sales also, because we were about 84 
people in the month of March in the sales department. Even now, as we speak, it's about 90. But 
all the people will now get relieved, and so we will be able to strengthen the sales team.

INR560 crores of disbursements have come from the sales team of about 98 people. So, of about 
average 90 people. In terms of that, the comparison, last year was for the full year, the sales team 
has contributed about INR868 crores. 
 
Basically, even without much of an addition in that team, the contribution has increased from 
the sales team, and now with additional staff that will be moving from the business to the sales 
division, we will be able to push further in terms of the of the sales team disbursements, and that 
should also support us in the Q3 and Q4.  
 
Same also in the sense that we have 28 branches, which are planned for the full year, as against 
that 25 branches have already been started, and they are operational with staffing also in place. 
Therefore, the contribution of these 25 branches will also come in Q3, Q4, which will support 
in our disbursement push. We hold the guidance of INR13,000 crores for disbursement and we'll 
push in Q3 and Q4 to cover up.  
 
The second thing is in terms of prepayment. You will see that in absolute value, last quarter, we 
had a slight increase and we had indicated that we are taking certain steps in terms of converting 
some regular excess payment customers to deposits or some alerts and all those things. Some 
impacts, we're starting to see in terms of the prepayments. July was a little high at INR655 crores, 
but then the next two months, it has dropped to below INR600 crores per month and for the full 
quarter, it has been much lower at 1,795 as compared to 1,857 in Q1 of this year. There has been 
an improvement in the prepayments.  
 
Plus, now with the rate hike, which has been there, the gap between the what the market is 
offering and what we are offering will come down because whereas there was a 25 basis points

the refinance as well as increase the proportion of refinance under the AHF component. This 
should help us positively, and the INR1,350 crores plus whatever is enhanced sanction can come, 
we will be drawing during the year.  
 
Last year, as a as a strategy, we had planned to draw the entire funds only in Q4, when normally 
the liquidity pressures are there and the rate is slightly elevated. But if the sanctions are on the 
higher side, we will probably start drawing this year from the Q3 itself, so that we can enjoy the 
lower rate also. In terms of the undrawn sanctions, we are having close to INR2,500 crores of 
undrawn sanctions, which are also there to support the business. In terms of the rate hike, as I 
mentioned, we've already passed on, effective 8th of October, 10 basis points for our housing 
customers.  
 
Basically, our endeavor will be to ensure that our NIM and spread and NIM stays protected. Our 
guidance of 2.75 and 3.75 for spread and NIM, whereas we have been operating around 2.8 and 
3.8. We should continue to protect our spread and NIM, and we are confident during the year, 
we should be able to maintain that because net impact of the rate hike would be that on a 65% 
of our liability side, we are impacted by this repo rate as well or by the T-bill rate. To that effect, 
it will be on the entire book, it will be about 12 to 13 basis points increase, which will be there. 
As against which, we have already increased 10 basis points.  
 
As you know, last year also, when the rates were coming down, we did it in four parts of 10 
basis points, 15 basis points, 15 basis points and 10 basis points. Same way the next hike, maybe 
we may look at a 15 so that we can average out to about 12 to 13 basis points. So, indirectly, 
what I'm trying to say that the NIM and spread, we will continue to maintain at 2.75 and 3.75 
plus, and that will be the thing. 
In terms of delinquency, our overall delinquency has not been impacted much, only there's a 
little bit of an increase in the SMA-0, which also is mainly because of the methodology of 
computation or flagging of this cases. So, basically, we had a old system which was computing 
the overdues or outstanding up to the end of the month, whereas here this is on a daily basis. 
So, if there are customers, many times for very, very small amounts, what was told to the 
customer five days back, the customer pays today, but the five days interest is becoming a lag. 
So we are slightly changing the process and all those things to see that we can communicate to

points. Generally also, you will see that in H2, there is a reduction in our gross NPA. So that

will come in the second half, so then we'll be under more comfortable position.

regulation or a guideline regarding this the reporting of disbursements as netting off the 
cancellations during the quarter, and the cancellations of the DD which have been from the date 
of the end of the quarter to the date of reporting. So that we have already implemented in this 
quarter, and we have netted off 29 crores from our disbursements, otherwise where the customers 
have been handed over the disbursements. 
The second thing is regarding the wage bill, where we have not had a problem in either of the 
two cases, where all our staff, we are having a salary more than 25,000. So even the joining 
entry-level salary starts from about 36,000. So basically, that is not impacting. And second thing 
is again, earlier last quarter also we had indicated, our basic plus DA is more than 50% of the 
total package. So that is also no impact on the company. 
The third is more of a prospective or a likely impact, which is because of the insurance discussion 
paper, or the insurance commissions have come down, are proposed to be brought down 
drastically. There also, in fact, the entire year last year, our commission from insurance business 
was only to the tune of about 12 and odd crores, which is less than 1% of our PBT of INR1,304 
crores of last year. 
So basically, even if it is implemented in the way it is has been shared or publicized in the media, 
it would not have any meaningful impact in terms of our profitability or anything, because the 
contribution of the insurance income is premium income is very, very low for us. So basically, 
these are the highlights of the quarter. We can open up to -- for question-answer. And once again,
